Biophysically Realistic 3-Axis Musculoskeletal Head–Neck Stabilization via Vestibulocollic (VCR) and Cervicocollic (CCR) Reflexes, Sensor Fusion, and Efference Copy Cancellation

Utku Oğuzman  |  Thesis Advisor: Prof. Dr. Murat Perit Çakır  ·  Department of Cognitive Science, Graduate School of Informatics, METU, Ankara

1. Stabilization Problem & Sensory-Driven Control

Stabilizing the human head in 3D space during translational and rotational trunk perturbations requires controlling an inherently unstable 6-DOF double-inverted cervical pendulum (C0–C2 & C2–T1) under strict biological timing, anatomical, and actuator constraints:

  • Gravitational & Anatomical Asymmetry: Anterior skull COM produces $+4.24\,\text{N}\cdot\text{m}$ resting flexion torque; 40 extensors ($49.5\,\text{N}\cdot\text{m}$) outweigh 24 flexors ($16.0\,\text{N}\cdot\text{m}$) $3.09:1$, while oblique muscles cross-couple Pitch, Roll, and Yaw and can induce intervertebral S-buckling ($q_1-q_2$).
  • Pull-Only Hill-Type Actuation & Resting Equilibrium: 72 musculotendon units (Millard12Eq) cannot push ($u_i \ge u_{\min,i}$) and introduce $\sim 30\text{–}50\,\text{ms}$ activation–contraction phase lag; resting co-contraction ($\mathbf{u}_{\min}$) is solved within 4 human cervical EMG bands to maintain static equilibrium.
  • Multi-Loop Axonal Conduction Latencies: Conduction delays span $1.0\text{–}14.5\,\text{ms}$ across five anatomical segments, closing three distinct feedback loops: Spinal VCR ($10\,\text{ms}$), Spinal CCR ($15\,\text{ms}$), and Cortical Control ($40\,\text{ms}$).
  • Sensory Ambiguity & Self-Motion Cancellation: Otoliths sense gravitoinertial specific force ($\mathbf{a}-\mathbf{g}$) rather than tilt alone, while fusimotor $\gamma$-drive alters spindle gain—requiring cerebellar efference copy cancellation and parallel reference-spindle subtraction.
  • 3-Axis Inertia Mismatch & Nonlinear Rectification: Pitch, Roll, and Yaw differ sharply in effective head–neck inertia; because pull-only muscles half-wave rectify spikes above $\mathbf{u}_{\min}$, unattenuated high-frequency noise rectifies into DC co-contraction drift.

Peripheral Mechanoreceptor Feedback: All 3D head orientation, angular velocity, and 6-DOF intervertebral neck posture estimates are reconstructed strictly from noisy dual-stream vestibular and intrafusal muscle spindle afferents rather than reading simulator coordinates directly.

2. Musculoskeletal Neck Model & Motion Rig

3. Five-Subsystem Delay-Compensated Neuromotor Control Architecture

13-Branch Delay & Lead Map

4. Simplified Subsystem Breakdown (Sub1 – Sub5)

Sub1 · Proprioception & CCR

Intrafusal Spindles (1A): 72 Mileusnic (2006) 3-fiber (bag1/bag2/chain) Ia & II units subtract $\gamma_{\text{dyn}}/\gamma_{\text{stat}}$ fusimotor drive via parallel reference spindles.

6-DOF Decoder: $\mathbf{K}_6 = -(J_6 J_6^\top + \lambda I_6)^{-1} J_6$ reconstructs all 6 cervical joint angles & velocities.

Spinal CCR (1B): C1–C8 per-muscle stretch reflex ($p_{\text{ccr}}$) with 3D isotropic scaling & reciprocal inhibition ($0\,\text{ms}$ local compute).

Sub2 · Vestibular & VCR

Dual-Stream Labyrinth (2A): 6 non-orthogonal semicircular canals + 3D otoliths split into irregular ($2.0\,\text{ms}$, high phase lead) and regular ($3.0\,\text{ms}$, Luenberger inverse for $1.0g$ gravity) afferents.

Brainstem VCR (2B): Strictly proper 2nd-order filters ($H_{\text{ton}}, H_{\text{sc}}, H_{\text{phas}}$, zero $D=0$) with deadbands drive fast head-in-space damping via MVST ($2.5\,\text{ms}$).

Sub3 · Cerebellar Observer

SE₂(3) Mahony Fusion: Combines canal $\hat{\boldsymbol{\omega}}_{\text{Luen}}$, otolith gravity, and spindle posture:

$\boldsymbol{\omega}_{\text{fuse}} = \hat{\boldsymbol{\omega}}_{\text{Luen}} + K_o(\tilde{\mathbf{u}}_{\text{oto}} \times \hat{R}^\top \mathbf{e}_y) + K_p\hat{R}^\top(\tilde{\boldsymbol{\theta}}_{\text{prop}} - \hat{\boldsymbol{\theta}})$

Efference Cancellation: Subtracts expected volitional & gravity acceleration ($\mathbf{c}_{\text{eff}}$) via the matched irregular otolith operator ($13\,\text{ms}$).

Sub4 · M1 Cortex & Thalamus

5-DOF Cortical Control: $2\times 2$ weighted IK ($\tau_{\text{traj}}=0.28\,\text{s}$) for P/R/Y + C1 shift with voluntary impedance, stiffness FF & $\mathrm{SE}_2(3)$ washout ($2\,\text{Hz}$ LPF).

Causal Tract Leads: Descending tracts ($9\text{–}14.5\,\text{ms}$) and all 13 central branches apply sender-side biproper leads:

$C_{\text{lead}}(s) = \frac{1 + (\tau_d + \tau_p)s}{1 + \tau_p s},\; \tau_p = \max(\tau_{\text{lead,pole}},\, 0.5\,\tau_d)$

Sub5 · Lamina IX Spinal Pool

Anti-Buckling + 6-DOF QP: Sums $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\text{vol}} + \boldsymbol{\tau}_{\text{vcr}} + \boldsymbol{\tau}_{\text{dec}}$ with $q_1-q_2$ nullspace damping ($K_{p,b}, K_{d,b,a}$) into $\min \frac{1}{2}\|\Delta\mathbf{u}\|_2^2$ s.t. $(J_6 F_{\max})\Delta\mathbf{u} = \boldsymbol{\tau}_{\text{des}} \mp \boldsymbol{\tau}_{\text{buckle}}$.

Ventral Root Out: Clamps $\mathbf{u}_\alpha + \mathbf{u}_{\text{ccr}}$ above $\mathbf{u}_{\min}$ with per-axis $\tau_{\text{lead,pole}}$ to drive 72 $\alpha/\gamma$ motoneurons ($2.5\,\text{ms}$).

5. Frequency-Response Validation Against Human Perturbation Benchmarks

6. Key Takeaways & Ongoing Work

  • Unified 3-Axis Stabilization: Combining strictly proper VCR, 3D-isotropic spinal CCR, and $SE_2(3)$ Mahony fusion reproduces human-like Pitch, Roll, and Yaw frequency responses simultaneously on a 72-muscle OpenSim plant.
  • Sensory-Only State Reconstruction: Attitude, angular velocity, and 6-DOF intervertebral posture are decoded solely from noisy vestibular and spindle afferents without direct coordinate access.
  • Minimal Axis Decoupling: Decoupling only 3 axis-level parameters ($\tau_{\text{lead,pole}}$, $p_{\text{ccr}}$, $K_{d,\text{buckle}}$) resolves Roll/Yaw inertia mismatch without per-muscle parameter explosion.
  • Causal Delay Compensation: Separating exact axonal conduction delays from sender-side biproper lead compensators preserves phase margin across 13 tracts without numerical stiffness.
  • Ongoing Work: Integrating active extraocular eye plants for coordinated head–eye gaze shifts and evaluating perturbation robustness across broader trunk-motion profiles.

Key Literature & References

  • Happee et al. (2017): Dynamic human head–neck stabilization under anterior-posterior seat perturbations (APEO pitch benchmark).
  • Happee et al. (2023): Lateral roll (LatEC) and axial yaw (YawMA) sensory integration in human head–neck control.
  • Mileusnic et al. (2006): Biophysical intrafusal muscle spindle model (bag1/bag2/chain Ia & II afferents with $\gamma$-fusimotor modulation).
  • Schneider et al. (2015) & Cullen (2012): Regular/irregular vestibular canal and otolith dynamics; cerebellar efference cancellation of self-motion.
  • Mahony et al. (2008): Nonlinear complementary attitude filters on SO(3) and SE₂(3) for multi-rate inertial sensor fusion.
  • Mortensen et al. (2018): OpenSim head-and-neck musculoskeletal model with hyoid musculature (HYOID 72-muscle 6-DOF cervical plant).
  • Vasavada et al. (1998) & Millard et al. (2013): Cervical muscle moment-arm geometry and equilibrium Hill-type muscle dynamics in OpenSim.
  • Keshner et al. (1989) & Falla et al. (2004): Surface EMG co-contraction envelopes and directional cervical muscle activation patterns.
